sections.html:
Tyler taxes are billed by Smith County, which collects for every taxing unit inside the county. Visit 1517 W. Front St., Tyler, TX 75702, write to P.O. Box 2011, or call (903) 590-2920. The office staffs its counter from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. with no lunch closure.

One Tyler bill can carry several lines: the city, Smith County, Tyler Junior College and a school district. The school district depends on the address, since some Tyler properties sit in Whitehouse ISD or Chapel Hill ISD instead of Tyler ISD. Your statement shows which one applies to you.

sections.h2: Tyler property tax rates, tax year 2026
sections.html:
These are the 2026 figures, each stated per $100 of value: $0.242063 for the city, $0.374088 for Smith County, $0.210312 for Tyler Junior College and $0.835000 for Tyler ISD.

Addresses served by Whitehouse ISD (0.964900) or Chapel Hill ISD (1.072900) use those school rates instead. Call the tax office to confirm the rate on your exact parcel.

Tyler has cut its city rate by more than 50 percent since the mid 1990s. It started at $0.5336 in 1994-95 and bottomed out at $0.1990 in 2007-08. It rose to $0.2699 in 2021-22, then fell each year to $0.236452 in 2025-26.

This year's 2026-27 rate of $0.242063 is higher than last year's and above the city's no-new-revenue rate of 0.232965. The city also commits two cents of its rate to the street fund, equal to $2.4 million.

  • 1994-95: $0.5336
  • 2007-08: $0.1990
  • 2021-22: $0.2699
  • 2025-26: $0.236452
  • 2026-27: $0.242063

Most Tyler-area rates fell from 2022 to 2026 while the county's rose.

  • Smith County: 0.330000 in 2022, 0.347264 in 2023, 0.364231 in 2024 and 2025, then 0.374088 in 2026.
  • Tyler ISD: 1.179300 in 2022, 0.960000 in 2023, 0.910000 in 2024, 0.845000 in 2025 and 0.835000 in 2026.
  • Tyler Junior College: 0.188001 in 2022, then 0.185068 in 2025 and 0.210312 in 2026.
  • City of Tyler: 0.261850 in 2022 and 0.242063 in 2026.

The statement you receive shows your exact numbers.

Tyler's sales tax rate is 8.25 percent. That splits into 6.25 percent for the State of Texas, 1 percent for the city's general fund, 0.5 percent for Tyler's One Half Cent Sales Tax Corporation and 0.5 percent for Smith County.

Nightly rentals owe hotel occupancy tax and short-term rental tax, paid through the city's portal at tylertx.hdlgov.com. A house that was ever rented that way is worth a call to the city finance department before listing, to rule out unpaid occupancy tax.

About 113,723 people live in Tyler, a 7.4 percent increase since 2020. Just over half of homes, 55.4 percent, are owner-occupied, and the median home value is $235,300. Renters pay a median of $1,252 a month, and owners spend $1,743 with a loan or $664 without. Moderate prices mean the school exemption takes a meaningful bite out of a typical bill.

Bills go out around October 1 and can be paid right away. You have until January 31 without penalty, and February 1 makes an unpaid bill delinquent.

Delinquency brings a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest. Penalty rises a point each month until July 1 puts it at 12 percent, while interest continues at one percent monthly. A unit's collection attorney can tack on up to 20 percent. Some homeowners can split the bill, paying once by November 30 and the rest by June 30 of the following year. Ask the Smith County office whether you qualify.

Every school district takes $140,000 off a homestead's value, and owners 65 or older, or disabled, get $60,000 more off the school value. File with the appraisal district before May 1 for most exemptions.

State law adds these protections for Tyler homes:

  • A 10 percent annual cap on appraised value increases for a residence homestead, starting the year after the exemption is first qualified.
  • A school-tax ceiling for seniors and disabled owners that can move with them to a new Texas homestead.
  • Disabled veteran exemptions of up to $5,000, $7,500, $10,000 or $12,000 depending on rating, and a total exemption for a 100 percent disabled veteran's homestead.

Cities, counties and colleges may add local exemptions. Ask the Smith County Appraisal District for the current local percentages.

To contest your value, file with the appraisal review board by May 15, or within 30 days of receiving your notice if that is later. Homestead notices for single-family houses go out near April 1, and hearings begin about mid May.

Unhappy with the ruling? Options include district court, binding arbitration, or a SOAH hearing if the board value tops $1,000,000. Keep paying: an appeal never pauses the bill, and you owe at least the undisputed tax by the delinquency date.

Texas puts a lien on the property each January 1 for that year's tax, and whoever owns it that day is liable. Your sale contract spells out who covers which share of the bill at closing.

Selling partway through the year? Get the amount due from the Smith County Tax Office in writing before closing. The title company pays it from your proceeds. A cash sale works the same way, because back tax must be cleared for title to pass.

Your exemption does not pass to the buyer automatically. If you never held one, a buyer closing after January 1 can apply for the rest of that year. Heirs with no recorded deed file an ownership affidavit and a death certificate.

faqs.q: What is the City of Tyler property tax rate?
faqs.a: $0.242063 per $100 for 2026-2027, though county, junior college and school district rates are added to your full bill.

faqs.q: Where do Tyler homeowners pay their tax?
faqs.a: At the Smith County Tax Office, 1517 W. Front St., Tyler, phone (903) 590-2920. That one office takes payment for the city and every other jurisdiction in the county.

faqs.q: When do Tyler property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On February 1, after the January 31 deadline. A 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest is added to what is still owed.

faqs.q: Is every Tyler address in Tyler ISD?
faqs.a: No. A few properties within Tyler belong to Whitehouse ISD or Chapel Hill ISD. Your statement names your district.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Tyler?
faqs.a: The school portion is $140,000 off your home's value, with $60,000 extra for seniors and disabled owners. City and county amounts come from the Smith County Appraisal District.
